lessons.title: Introduction to Programming
lessons.description: Learn what programming is and why it matters
lessons.mission: Understand the basics of programming and how computers follow instructions
objectives: Understand what programming is
Learn how computers follow instructions
Write your first line of code
lessons.story: Think of programming like giving instructions to a robot. Just like you tell someone how to make a sandwich step by step, programming tells a computer exactly what to do. Every app, game, and website you've ever used was created by someone writing instructions for a computer to follow.

comparisons.example: Giving step-by-step instructions to a robot
Following instructions to build a LEGO set
Following a recipe to bake a cake

lessons.explanation: Programming is the art of telling a computer what to do. You write code, which is a set of instructions, and the computer follows them exactly. It's like writing a recipe - if you follow the instructions correctly, you get the result you want.

codeExamples.title: Your First Program
codeExamples.code:
console.log('Hello, World!');
// This prints a message to the console
codeExamples.explanation: This is your first program! It prints 'Hello, World!' to the console. The console is like a message board where your program can show information.

codeExamples.title: Using Comments
codeExamples.explanation: Comments are notes in your code that computers ignore. They help you and others understand what your code does.

interactiveExample.description: Click the button to run your first program!

flashcards.question: What is programming?
flashcards.answer: Programming is writing instructions for a computer to follow

flashcards.question: What is code?
flashcards.answer: Code is the set of instructions you write for a computer

flashcards.question: What is a comment?
flashcards.answer: A comment is text in code that computers ignore - it's for humans to read

quiz.question: What is programming?
quiz.correct: Writing instructions for a computer

quiz.question: What does console.log do?
options: Prints a message to the console
quiz.correct: Prints a message to the console

quiz.question: What is a comment in code?
options: Text that runs on the computer
quiz.correct: Text that computers ignore

lessons.summary: Programming is the process of writing instructions for computers. You use code to tell computers exactly what to do. Every program starts with a simple idea and turns into a set of instructions that a computer can follow. Comments help you document your code for yourself and others.

lessons.title: JavaScript Introduction
lessons.description: Get started with JavaScript programming
lessons.mission: Learn what JavaScript is and write your first interactive code
objectives: Understand what JavaScript is used for
Write your first JavaScript code
See the result in the console
lessons.story: JavaScript is like the magic that makes websites interactive. When you click a button and something happens on a webpage, that's JavaScript at work. It's the language that powers the modern web, from simple animations to complex applications like Google Maps and Facebook.
lessons.storyTitle: JavaScript - The Magic of the Web

comparisons.example: The engine that powers interactive websites
Making a game respond when you press a key
A magician performing tricks on stage

lessons.explanation: JavaScript is a programming language that runs in web browsers. It's used to create interactive web pages, web applications, games, and even server-side applications. Everything from simple animations to complex applications like Google Maps is built with JavaScript.

codeExamples.title: Your First JavaScript
codeExamples.explanation: This creates a variable called 'message' and prints it to the console. Variables are like labeled boxes where you can store information.

codeExamples.title: Simple Math
codeExamples.explanation: JavaScript can do math too! Here we add two numbers and display the result.

interactiveExample.description: Click to see JavaScript in action!

flashcards.question: What is JavaScript used for?
flashcards.answer: Creating interactive web pages and web applications

flashcards.question: Where does JavaScript run?
flashcards.answer: In web browsers and on servers

flashcards.question: What is a variable?
flashcards.answer: A variable is like a labeled box that stores information

quiz.question: What is JavaScript used for?
quiz.correct: Creating interactive web applications

quiz.question: Where does JavaScript typically run?
quiz.correct: In a web browser

quiz.question: What is a variable in JavaScript?
quiz.correct: A container for storing data

lessons.summary: JavaScript is a powerful programming language used to create interactive websites and applications. It runs in web browsers and can do everything from simple animations to complex web applications. Variables are containers that store data, and you can use them to hold information like text, numbers, and more.

lessons.title: Variables - Storage Boxes
lessons.description: Learn how to store and manage data with variables
lessons.mission: Master variables and learn how to store different types of data
objectives: Understand what variables are
Learn how to declare variables
Store different types of data
Use variables in your code
lessons.story: Imagine you have a set of boxes in your room. Each box has a label, and you can put different things inside - books, toys, clothes. Variables in programming work exactly the same way! They're labeled boxes where you store information that you might need later.

comparisons.example: A labeled box that stores information

lessons.explanation: Variables are containers that store data. You give them a name and put a value inside. Think of them like boxes with labels - you can put things in, take things out, and change what's inside whenever you want.

codeExamples.title: Creating Variables
codeExamples.explanation: Variables can store different types of data: text (strings), numbers, booleans (true/false), and arrays (lists of items).

codeExamples.title: Changing Variables
codeExamples.explanation: You can change what's stored in a variable at any time. You can even use the current value to compute a new value.

interactiveExample.description: Click to see variables in action!

flashcards.question: What is a variable?
flashcards.answer: A container that stores data with a name

flashcards.question: What types of data can variables store?
flashcards.answer: Strings (text), Numbers, Booleans, Arrays, Objects, and more

flashcards.question: Can you change a variable's value?
flashcards.answer: Yes! You can assign a new value to a variable anytime

quiz.question: What is a variable?
quiz.correct: A container for storing data

quiz.question: Which is a valid variable name in JavaScript?
quiz.correct: myVariable
Adds 3 to x, making it 8

lessons.summary: Variables are containers that store data. They can hold different types of information like text, numbers, true/false values, and lists. You can create variables, give them values, and change those values whenever you need. This is the foundation of programming!

lessons.title: Data Types - Different Types of Information
lessons.description: Explore the different types of data in JavaScript
lessons.mission: Understand the different data types and when to use each one
objectives: Learn the main data types in JavaScript
Understand strings, numbers, and booleans
Work with arrays and objects
Use type checking in your code
lessons.story: Think about how you organize information in real life. You have names (text), ages (numbers), yes/no answers (booleans), and shopping lists (arrays). JavaScript organizes information in similar ways using different data types.
lessons.explanation: Data types tell JavaScript what kind of information you're working with. Strings are text, numbers are for math, booleans are for true/false, arrays are for lists, and objects are for storing related information together.

codeExamples.title: Working with Different Types
codeExamples.explanation: JavaScript has several built-in data types. Strings are text, numbers are for math, booleans are for true/false, arrays are for lists, and objects are for organizing related data.

codeExamples.title: Checking Types
codeExamples.explanation: You can use the typeof operator to check what type of data a variable contains.

interactiveExample.description: Click to see different data types in action!

flashcards.question: What is a String?
flashcards.answer: A sequence of characters used for text

quiz.question: What type of data is 'Hello World'?
quiz.correct: String

quiz.question: What type of data is true or false?
quiz.correct: Boolean

quiz.question: What is an Array used for?
quiz.correct: Storing a list of items

lessons.summary: JavaScript has different data types for different kinds of information: strings for text, numbers for math, booleans for true/false, arrays for lists, and objects for organizing related data. Understanding data types helps you choose the right type for your information.

lessons.title: Operators - Performing Actions
lessons.description: Learn how to perform actions with operators
lessons.mission: Master operators and use them to manipulate data
objectives: Understand arithmetic operators
Learn comparison operators
Work with logical operators
Combine operators in expressions
lessons.story: Think about how you use a calculator to add, subtract, multiply, and divide numbers. Operators in programming are like the buttons on a calculator - they let you perform operations on your data.
lessons.explanation: Operators are symbols that perform actions on your data. Arithmetic operators do math (+, -, *, /). Comparison operators compare values (>, <, ==, ===). Logical operators combine conditions (&&, ||, !).

codeExamples.title: Arithmetic Operators
codeExamples.code:
let a = 10;
let b = 3;

console.log('Addition:', a + b);      // 13
console.log('Subtraction:', a - b);   // 7
console.log('Multiplication:', a * b); // 30
console.log('Division:', a / b);       // 3.33...
console.log('Modulus (remainder):', a % b); // 1
console.log('Exponent:', a ** b);      // 1000
codeExamples.explanation: Arithmetic operators perform mathematical operations. The modulus operator (%) gives you the remainder of a division.

codeExamples.title: Comparison Operators
codeExamples.explanation: Comparison operators compare two values and return true or false. The strict equality operator (===) also checks that the data types match.

codeExamples.title: Logical Operators
codeExamples.explanation: Logical operators combine conditions. AND (&&) requires both to be true. OR (||) requires at least one to be true. NOT (!) reverses the value.

interactiveExample.description: Click to see operators in action!

flashcards.question: What does the === operator do?
flashcards.answer: Checks if two values are equal AND the same type

flashcards.question: What does the && operator do?
flashcards.answer: Returns true only if both conditions are true

quiz.question: What does 10 + 5 equal?
What does 10 % 3 equal? (Hint: % is modulus - remainder)
What is the result of 5 > 3?
quiz.correct: true

quiz.question: What does true && false equal?
quiz.correct: false

lessons.summary: Operators are symbols that perform actions on your data. Arithmetic operators (+, -, *, /, %) do math. Comparison operators (>, <, ==, ===) compare values. Logical operators (&&, ||, !) combine conditions. Master these, and you can manipulate data effectively!
